title: J.D. LaRock:
title_q: “The Students Are Showing Us Where to Go”
title_short: J.D. · Students Show Us Where to Go
headline: NFTE did not stop students from using AI. It followed them.
story: J.D. LaRock tells what NFTE saw in the last four years. First students used AI tools for their business plans. NFTE asked itself honestly: is that good? It chose to see what they could do. Then students started to build businesses based in AI.
His point: encourage learners to lean into what they love. Nobody really knows where AI goes, but the flip side of skepticism is the possibility for more. Open and hopeful, never afraid of AI.

Machine transcript (Oct 7) of Panel › L012C003_260922M0.MXF, Track 1. Times are mm:ss in L012C003. Every line here is J.D. LaRock. The machine writes "Nifty" and "Mifty" for NFTE, and "chat and plot" at 46:05 is unclear.
[45:43] It reminds me of something that we have consistently seen over the past few years in our collective
[45:48] work with Nifty and all of our organizations.
[45:52] About four years ago, we started seeing young people do two things with their business
[45:58] ideas and business plan.
[46:00] Very clear that they were beginning to use a whole range of different AI tools.
[46:04] And of course, you know there are many.
[46:05] It's not just chat and plot, but there's all the design-oriented tools, the financial
[46:09] tools.
[46:09] There's not actually a lot of helpful tools that make presentations look better and all of this kind of stuff.
[46:16] They were starting to use that.
[46:18] So as an organization we had to, you know, ask ourselves, is that good?
[46:23] I was like, I don't know, let's see what they can do with it.
[46:26] The other thing that happened was that steadily, more and more each year, students were proposing businesses that were based in AI.
[46:33] So in the same way that the Internet Revolution brought on platform-based businesses, the
[46:38] same way that app development and the iPhone brought on a whole wave of app-based businesses,
[46:43] we just saw our student competitors naturally proposing and developing businesses that had
[46:49] AI as the basis of the business in some way, shape, or form.
[46:54] Either that is AI in the context of some sort of physical technology that they were
[46:59] developing, or AI as the basis of, let's say, a chatbot or service type of business.
[47:05] So we saw all of that.
[47:07] So I think at a certain point, and I imagine all of you agree, we just said at Mifty, well,
[47:13] the students are showing us where to go here, and we probably should not stop them because
[47:20] it's a good thing to encourage learners to pursue learning and to lean into the things
[47:25] that they're passionate about.
[47:26] So we, you know, yes, we put some parameters around it,
[47:30] but we generally let it go.
[47:32] And what we've seen is that two things,
[47:36] as we discussed before, there has been this very evident,
[47:40] meaningful division point, this threshold,
[47:43] between the students who use AI in a responsible way,
[47:47] in a productive way, and can still demonstrate
[47:50] learning authentically in sophisticated ways.
[47:54] Yeah, and so we have just leaned into that.
[47:57] More comments?
[51:06] Good.
[51:06] I'll just close this out with this.
[51:09] One mindset domain that I think is important in this day and age, and frankly I think our conversation kind of brought it out, is skepticism.
[51:20] Skepticism as an important mindset domain for this day and age, because it's so easy
[51:29] to get caught up in the daily barrage of news and fatalistic predictions and prognostications
[51:40] of what all of this will mean.
[51:42] Let's just admit that no one really knows.
[51:46] However, let's also admit that's where the skepticism comes in.
[51:51] But the flip side of skepticism is the possibility for more.
[51:56] And I think that's what we have explored here today.
[52:00] So thank you for being a part of this conversation.
[52:02] Special thanks to all the other young people in the audience.
